related_questions.question: What is the property tax forfeiture process in Minnesota?
related_questions.snippet: The process by which the state takes ownership of real property due to unpaid property taxes. In Minnesota, the process generally takes four years from the time the taxes were due (taxes due in 2022 are subject to forfeiture in 2026). It also includes several stages including a period of redemption.

text_blocks.snippet: In Minnesota, tax-forfeited land refers to property where the title has been acquired by the State of Minnesota due to non-payment of property taxes. This happens after a period of delinquency, typically three years, during which the owner can redeem the property by paying the delinquent taxes. If the taxes remain unpaid, the property is forfeited to the state.
snippet_highlighted_words: property where the title has been acquired by the State of Minnesota due to non-payment of property taxes

list.title: Delinquent Taxes:
list.snippet: Property owners are responsible for paying property taxes on their land. If these taxes are not paid, they become delinquent.

list.title: Redemption Period:
list.snippet: Minnesota law provides a period of time (usually three years) during which the property owner can pay the delinquent taxes and "redeem" their property, preventing forfeiture.

list.title: Forfeiture:
list.snippet: If the taxes remain unpaid at the end of the redemption period, the property is forfeited to the State of Minnesota in trust.

list.title: State in Trust:
list.snippet: The State of Minnesota holds forfeited land in trust, usually for the benefit of local taxing districts (counties, cities, townships, etc.).

list.title: County Management:
list.snippet: The forfeited land is then managed by the county where the property is located.

list.title: Sale or Other Use:
list.snippet: The county can then sell the land, lease it, or use it for public purposes.

list.title: Hunting and Camping:
list.snippet: In many counties, tax-forfeited land can be used for hunting and camping, subject to certain rules and regulations.

list.title: Contacting the County:
list.snippet: If you are interested in purchasing tax-forfeited land, you should contact the county auditor or land department in the county where the land is located, according to the Minnesota DNR.
